materials.title: The ticket in the coat pocket
materials.text:
Before a train journey, I checked my phone ticket, charger and wallet. I felt unusually ____1____. Then Mum asked whether I had checked the station name.

"Of course," I replied, though I had only checked the departure ____2____. The train left from our town’s smaller station across the river. I had planned to walk to the main station near our house.

Mum agreed to drive me there. I set an earlier alarm and placed my coat beside the door. The journey now seemed safely ____3____ again.

At breakfast, Mum handed me an old ticket from my coat pocket. It was two years old. "At least this one tells you where it starts," she said, pointing to the ____4____ printed above the date.

I almost threw it away. Then I noticed a small pencil ____5____ on the back: "Window seat. First time travelling alone." I remembered writing it. The ticket had become more than evidence that I had paid a ____6____.

I put the old ticket in a drawer, separate from the things I needed that morning. A memory was worth keeping, but it would not ____7____ the barrier at the station. I needed the current phone code.

We arrived with time to spare. I checked the platform, found my carriage and sat by the window. The old note had reminded me how ____8____ I had felt on my first solo trip. Today I was less afraid, although clearly not beyond making a ____9____.

Before departure, I sent Mum a message: right station, right train.  I began a new note about the journey, recording the view rather than simply the ____10____. The details would help me remember it, while the booking would do its ____11____ job for travel. Keeping them ____12____ made both easier to use. Then the train moved. I put the phone away and watched the river ____13____ beneath the bridge. For once, I had finished ____14____ and could enjoy being on my ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Repeated packing checks produce a feeling of being organised. Fame/hunger/lateness are not the resulting preparedness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: He checked departure time but not station. Price/colour/passenger do not complete the schedule detail contrasted.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The revised arrangement feels settled. The journey is not cancelled, forgotten or promoted.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The station name is a place printed above the date. Cost/weather/number do not identify where the trip starts.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The quoted words form a pencil note. It is neither hole, price nor picture.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: A train ticket proves payment of a fare. Visit/compliment/salary are not the passenger charge.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: An obsolete ticket cannot open the current barrier. Paint/repair/locate are not its admission function.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Less afraid today recalls previous nervousness. Wealth/boredom/anger are not the contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: He nearly chose the wrong station, a mistake. Promise/meal/profit do not describe it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The personal note records views beyond booking information. Weather/scenery/river are aspects of the viewed journey, not the travel record contrasted.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The booking serves the practical travel function. Imaginary/musical/historical do not describe current admission.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Separate memory note and current booking are kept distinct. Identical contradicts the different functions; secrecy/hiding is not the useful separation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: From the moving train the river passes beneath the bridge in view. Freezing/returning/disappearing are not stated physical changes.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Preparations are complete as the trip begins. Sleeping/forgetting are not the checks, and travelling is just starting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: On my way means travelling towards the destination. Feet would imply standing despite the stated seat, guard implies vigilance rather than relaxed enjoyment and on my side does not describe a journey.

materials.title: The moving shadow
materials.text:
A shadow is an area receiving less light because something blocks the source. Its outline depends on the ____1____ between the light, the blocking object and the surface where we see it.

Move a lamp while keeping a small object still, and its shadow may change position. Moving the object also changes it. The shadow is therefore not a fixed ____2____ of the object's shape alone.

Outdoors, sunlight provides a familiar example. As the sun's apparent position in the sky changes during the day, the direction and length of a vertical post's shadow also ____3____. A mark at one hour may not match the next.

Sundials use this movement, but are not read like modern clocks. A dial's design must relate to its location and ____4____. Turning it carelessly may make an attractive object that no longer tells time as intended.

Clouds introduce another limitation. When direct sunlight is weak or absent, the shadow may be too ____5____ to read clearly. A sundial does not solve that problem by having more numbers printed around its edge.

Students might mark a post’s shadow at different times. They should keep the post ____6____ and record when each mark is made. Otherwise, a change caused by moving the post could be ____7____ for a change caused by the sun's apparent movement.

The observations can show a pattern without providing every part of an astronomical explanation. A flat drawing of the marks is a ____8____ of what happened at that site, not a model of the entire sky. It gains value when its ____9____ are stated clearly.

Examining a shadow connects a visible effect with an arrangement not fully revealed by its outline. The question is not only what ____10____ the patch has, but why it appears there. Changing one part of the arrangement while keeping others stable makes that relationship easier to ____11____. The ordinary patch on the ground becomes ____12____ for inquiry. Its movement is neither a conscious choice nor a ____13____ by the object; it follows the changing conditions of illumination. With those conditions considered, the shadow becomes less ____14____ without becoming less ____15____ to observe.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Arrangement includes positions of all three elements. Agreement/competition imply agents and distance alone omits direction and relative placement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The outline is not a property of object shape alone. Owner/surface/price do not describe the dependence being corrected.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Direction/length vary with sun position. They do not necessarily vanish or return during the stated change, and rest denies movement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Dial orientation relates it to sunlight and location. Decoration/popularity/ownership do not establish correct placement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Weak direct light makes an indistinct/faint shadow. Weight/size/straightness do not state poor visibility.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Keep the post stationary to isolate solar change. Temperature/cost/decoration are not the motion control.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Mistaken for means incorrectly attributed as another cause. The other participles do not form that identification meaning.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The drawing records local observations. It is not the cause, prediction or physical replacement of the sky.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Stating limits clarifies a local record’s scope. Colours/owners/prices do not define interpretive reach.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Shape is the visible outline to be explained. Purpose/name/memory do not identify that geometric effect.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Changing one factor systematically tests the relationship. Hiding/selling/ignoring do not investigate it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Observed movement supplies evidence for inquiry. Payment/permission/decoration are not empirical observations.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The sentence rejects conscious choice/decision by the object. Reflection/measurement/description do not name intentional agency here.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Explained conditions make it less mysterious. Visibility/usefulness/accuracy are not necessarily reduced by understanding.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Understanding need not reduce interest. Cost/portability/silence are not observational engagement.

materials.title: The programme without a biography
materials.text:
Composer Mara was asked to send a programme biography before introducing a new piece. She opened an old file containing a long list of prizes. It was accurate, yet it gave almost no ____1____ of what a listener might hear that evening.

She replaced the awards with a question: how a melody changes when different instruments ____2____ it. Cello and flute could give the same phrase different weight.

She worried it sounded like ____3____. Would listeners feel obliged to hear exactly what she had named? She added that the comparison was one route into the music, not a test with a correct ____4____.

The organiser read the draft and asked for a little basic information too. It still needed to identify the composer. Mara had moved from one ____5____ to another: first a list with no doorway into the music, then a discussion with almost no person attached.

They combined a brief factual paragraph with the introduction. The two sections served different ____6____, and neither had to carry everything. Mara removed a sentence that inflated a past workshop into a permanent ____7____.

She spoke briefly, then left space for the music. Afterwards, one listener described an image Mara had never ____8____. It concerned an exchange between viola and piano.

 Her introduction had not failed because it did not ____9____ the listener's response. It had offered a way to begin paying attention. What followed could belong partly to the listener.

Back home, she saved the revised biography in a new file. The old awards list remained available when a different occasion ____10____ it. She no longer expected one description to suit every ____11____. A programme, a funding application and a conversation after a concert asked different questions. Writing well about her work meant choosing information for the ____12____ at hand, while keeping the facts ____13____. The evening had not taught her to hide her achievements. It had taught her to give them an appropriate ____14____, rather than let them occupy the whole ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The list gives little indication of what the music sounds like. Guarantee/measurement/permission are stronger or different claims, not descriptive guidance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Instruments carry/play the melody. Repair/purchase/name do not describe musical transfer of the phrase.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: She worries listeners will feel obliged to follow instructions. Memories/invitations/questions do not convey that imposed hearing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A test has a correct answer. Ticket/instrument/biography do not complete the assessment metaphor.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: She moved between extremes: all CV and all music discussion. The other nouns are content/events, not the opposite imbalances.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Identity and musical access are different purposes. Composers/evenings/instruments do not name these functions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A workshop must not be inflated into a permanent appointment/post. An invitation is not a permanent job, rehearsal an event and melody musical content.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The listener supplies an image Mara had not imagined. Heard concerns sound, published/forgotten would imply prior possession not established.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The introduction need not determine/control the response. Describe/welcome/record do not name the assumed obligation to dictate interpretation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Another purpose may require the factual awards list. Rejection/forgetting/invention do not explain retaining it for use.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Different audiences/contexts need different descriptions. Instruments/composers/melodies are not readers of the same biography.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Occasion at hand names the present communication situation. Prize/notebook/address are not the event-purpose context.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Facts must remain accurate across different selections. Secrecy/length/identical wording are not that truth constraint.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: An appropriate place gives achievements proportionate space. Cost/owner/sound do not express position in the introduction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The whole page is programme space achievements might occupy. Orchestra/melody/career are not the textual space contrasted.
